record_type_quote: In this direct replication of Houben, Otgaar, Roelofs, and Merckelbach (Clinical Psychological Science, 6, 610–616, 2018), we tested whether making eye movements during memory recall increases susceptibility to creating false memories.

targets.authors: Houben, S. T., Otgaar, H., Roelofs, J., & Merckelbach, H.
targets.title: Lateral eye movements increase false memory rates.
targets.evidence_quote: In this direct replication of Houben, Otgaar, Roelofs, and Merckelbach (Clinical Psychological Science, 6, 610–616, 2018), we tested whether making eye movements during memory recall increases susceptibility to creating false memories.
targets.outcome_quote: In conclusion, the current experiment was a first direct replication of Houben et al. (2018), but failed to find the original study’s effect that making EMs during memory recall increases a person’s susceptibility to endorsing misinformation.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The overall conclusion explicitly says the original effect failed to replicate.

reasoning: Direct replication with a new undergraduate sample; the original-data correlations in a footnote are ancillary.
